text.p: Australia on Tuesday said Cambodian Second Prime Minister Hun Sen's military takeover was "revolutionary", but would not rule out eventually recognising his new government.

Prime Minister John Howard told reporters that Australia would closely monitor developments in Cambodia and remained prepared to evacuate Australians if the situation in the troubled Southeast Asian nation worsened.
"Hun Sen is not the authorised government...and obviously his behaviour has been, how shall one put it, of a revolutionary kind," Howard said.

"Obviously you have to wait and see how this situation unfolds and you have to mix a presumption of legitimacy against realism," said Howard, referring to Australia's future position towards the Hun Sen government.
Howard said Australia was disappointed at the breakdown of the 1991 Paris peace accords that ended three decades of war and civil strife in Cambodia.
"We are very disappointed that the peace process has broken down, but in the end it is a matter for the Cambodian people to work out," Howard said.

Australia has two military transport aircraft on standby at an airbase in Malaysia to evacuate Australians from Phnom Penh if fighting between forces loyal to Hun Sen, who is Cambodia's second prime minister, and royalist forces supporting First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh breaks out.

Fighting began on Saturday when Hun Sen sent in his forces against Ranariddh's men, and although it was over by Monday, sections of Phnom Penh remained lawless and violent as troops celebrated their victory with looting.
